_comment: Labelled calibration set for RAG threshold calibration (services/retrieval_calibration.py). Positives (relevant=true) are questions the shipped corpus SHOULD answer; negatives (relevant=false) are questions it should answer with NO guideline at all. Re-run after changing the corpus or the embedder: `python scripts/calibrate_retrieval.py`.
_negatives_note: The negatives deliberately come in TWO shapes. The administrative ones (wifi, parking, cafeteria) were always easy — no clinical vocabulary, nothing scores. The clinical ones (dengue, COPD, malaria, snakebite, eclampsia, thyroid storm, burns, alcohol withdrawal, ATT, neonatal jaundice) are the hard and honest case, and the reason DEF-4 reached the ward: they are real presentations on an Indian ward, they are written in fluent clinical language, and this corpus contains NOTHING about them. A retrieval stack that cannot say 'no guideline matched' to these will cite ventilator weaning to a dengue patient. Every clinical negative here was verified absent from both the built-in corpus (services/clinical_knowledge.CLINICAL_DOCUMENTS) and the loader corpus (server/corpus/) on 2026-08-14 — recheck when either grows, and MOVE a case to relevant=true rather than deleting it if the corpus starts covering that topic.
_expected_note: `expected` lists the document_ids that legitimately answer a positive query, and it is what lets the calibrator score EVERY hit instead of only the top one. Added 2026-08-15. Until then the harness read results[0] alone, so a relevant guideline at rank 2 was invisible to it — and a floor that dropped one moved no number the harness reported. That is how the first alert-shaped recalibration silently cost the UTI alert its antibiotic guideline (EXT-ID-002, 0.318, against a 0.341 floor); a test caught it, the harness did not. With every hit labelled, EXT-ID-002 entered the derivation and the floor came down to 0.31541 to keep it. Rules for maintaining these: list every document you would defend to a clinician as answering the query, INCLUDING ones that currently score too low to be cited (the loss then shows up as document-level recall rather than disappearing); label by clinical judgment against the corpus, never by copying what retrieval currently returns, which would make the calibration measure its own output. Negatives take no `expected` — by definition nothing answers them, so every candidate they return is a false positive and all of them are counted. An UNLABELLED positive still works and falls back to its top hit, but the run then reports `unlabelled_cases` so nobody reads its document-level numbers as truth.
_alert_shape_note: The third block is ALERT-SHAPED: the query the drafted-assessment lane and the prefetch warmer actually send, as services/retrieval_query.build_guideline_query composes it — working diagnosis, then the active problem list, then the NEWS2 drivers. Added 2026-08-15 with that builder, because until then BOTH lanes retrieved on the drivers alone and this set contained not one query of the shape the ward was really running (every case here was a clinician-typed question). A floor derived only from typed questions is a floor calibrated on a distribution the alert lane never produces. The last three cases are the DEGRADED shape — drivers with no condition named, which is what a patient with no diagnosis on record still gets — and they are labelled NEGATIVE: a query that does not say what the patient has cannot be answered by a condition-specific protocol, and citing one is DEF-4 itself.

cases._note: KNOWN MISS, deliberately left labelled positive. EXT-SEPSIS-003 (Sepsis Fluid Resuscitation & Vasopressors) does answer this and IS retrieved, but only at rank 2 with relevance 0.037 — below any defensible floor — while EXT-CARD-002 (heart failure) takes rank 1 at 0.043. So this query loses its evidence. That is a real recall cost of the floor and it belongs in the labelled set as a positive, visible, rather than relabelled away to make the numbers look clean.

The whole retrieved list peaks at relevance 0.0029 (top hit: DVT/VTE PROPHYLAXIS). Labelling an uncovered topic as a positive teaches the calibrator that near-zero relevance is acceptable, which is precisely how a floor gets derived too low to stop anything.
